```{r setup, include = FALSE}
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)

```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Krause_2016_ACT451840"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Krause_2016_ACT451840"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1111/bcp.12962> (open access, PMC4972157)

ACT-451840 (Actelion-451840) is an investigational antimalarial with a new
mechanism of action. Krause 2016 fitted a joint PK/PD model to data from an
induced blood-stage malaria (IBSM) challenge study and used it to predict the
number of once-daily doses that cures an infection.

# Population

Eight healthy, malaria-naive men (mean age 24 years, range 19-38; mean body
weight 77 kg, range 59-98; BMI 24, range 20-28 kg/m^2) were inoculated
intravenously with about 1800 viable *Plasmodium falciparum* 3D7-infected
erythrocytes. Four subjects were Caucasian, two Indian, one Asian and one
Native Hawaiian. On day 7 (168 h after inoculation), when parasitaemia had
reached about 1000 parasites/mL, every subject received a single 500 mg oral
dose of ACT-451840 as a suspension after a high-fat breakfast. Plasma drug
concentrations (LC-MS/MS, LLOQ 0.1 ng/mL) were sampled to 144 h after dosing and
parasitaemia (qPCR, LOD 64 parasites/mL) to rescue treatment with
artemether/lumefantrine on recrudescence. The study was run at Q-Pharm in
Brisbane, Australia. Demographics are from the Results section 'Subject
demographics' of Krause 2016; the paper has no demographics table.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Krause_2016_ACT451840")()$population`.

# Source trace

Every structural value comes from Krause 2016 Table 1 ('Final parameter
estimates'); the structural equation is the single displayed equation in the
Methods section 'PK/PD modelling'.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| `lka` (ka) | 0.23 1/h | Table 1 |
| `ltlag` (tlag) | 0.45 h | Table 1 |
| `lkel` (k) | 0.31 1/h | Table 1 |
| `lvc` (V/F) | 1337.89 L | Table 1 |
| `lk12` (k12) | 0.11 1/h | Table 1 |
| `lk21` (k21) | 0.03 1/h | Table 1 |
| `lrbase_parasites` (P0) | 0.11 parasites/mL | Table 1 |
| `lkgrow` (G) | 6.67 %/h = 0.0667 1/h | Table 1 (printed as 'unitless'; scale: see Assumptions) |
| `lemax` (D) | 18.09 %/h = 0.1809 1/h | Table 1 (printed as 'unitless'; scale: see Assumptions) |
| `lec50` (IC50) | 2.70 ng/mL | Table 1 |
| `lhill` (gamma) | 2.46 | Table 1 |
| IIV SDs: ka, tlag, k, V, k12, k21 | 0.14, 0.05, 0.29, 0.20, 0.06, 0.08 | Table 1, 'Random effects (standard deviations)'; variance = SD^2 |
| IIV SDs: P0, G, D, IC50, gamma | 1.18, 0.03, 0.04, 0.25, 0.08 | Table 1, same block |
| `addSd`, `propSd` (PK) | 4.38e-9 ng/mL, 0.265 | Table 1, 'Error terms' |
| `addSd_parasites`, `propSd_parasites` (PD) | 26.1 parasites/mL, 0.558 | Table 1, 'Error terms' |
| `d/dt(parasites) = parasites * (kgrow - emax * Cc^hill / (Cc^hill + ec50^hill))` | n/a | Methods, 'PK/PD modelling', displayed equation |
| PK structure (2-compartment, first-order absorption with lag) | n/a | Results, 'PK/PD modelling' |
| `parasites(0) = P0` at inoculation, 168 h before dosing | n/a | Methods (P0 definition) and Results (P0 'at time of inoculation, -168 h relative to drug administration') |
| Cure threshold 0.003 parasites/mL (simulation rule only) | n/a | Methods, 'Pharmacodynamics and statistical assessments' |

```{r model}
mod <- readModelDb("Krause_2016_ACT451840")
mod_typical <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)
```

Model time 0 is the inoculation; the drug is dosed at 168 h, the study
schedule. The figures below plot time relative to the first dose, as the paper
does.

```{r helpers}
cure_threshold <- 0.003 # parasites/mL, Krause 2016 Methods
t_dose1 <- 168

# One subject-arm event table: `n_dose` once-daily doses of `dose_mg` starting
# 168 h after inoculation, observed on the parasite state every `dt` hours.
make_arm <- function(n_sub, n_dose, dose_mg, id_offset, dt = 2, t_end = t_dose1 + 300) {
  ids <- id_offset + seq_len(n_sub)
  doses <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = ids, time = t_dose1 + 24 * (seq_len(n_dose) - 1)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(evid = 1L, amt = dose_mg, cmt = "depot")
  obs <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = ids, time = seq(0, t_end, by = dt)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(evid = 0L, amt = 0, cmt = "parasites")
  dplyr::bind_rows(doses, obs) |>
    dplyr::mutate(arm = sprintf("%d x %d mg", n_dose, dose_mg)) |>
    dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))
}

# The paper treats an infection as cured once parasitaemia falls below the
# threshold; from then on the trajectory is held at the threshold, which is the
# flat floor in Figures 5B and 6.
apply_cure <- function(sim) {
  sim |>
    dplyr::group_by(id) |>
    dplyr::arrange(time, .by_group = TRUE) |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      cured = cumsum(time >= t_dose1 & parasites < cure_threshold) > 0,
      parasites_plot = ifelse(cured, cure_threshold, parasites)
    ) |>
    dplyr::ungroup()
}
```

# Typical-value replication of Figure 5

```{r fig5-sim}
# One single-subject solve per regimen: the typical model has no omega, and
# rxode2 warns about a multi-subject solve without one.
sim_typ <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(1:4, function(n) {
  ev <- make_arm(1, n, 500, id_offset = n - 1, dt = 0.5)
  rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typical, events = ev, keep = "arm") |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    dplyr::mutate(id = n)
})) |>
  apply_cure() |>
  dplyr::mutate(time_rel = time - t_dose1)
```

```{r fig5, fig.height = 4}
p_pk <- ggplot(sim_typ, aes(time_rel, Cc, colour = arm)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(x = "Time after first dose (h)", y = "ACT-451840 (ng/mL)", colour = NULL,
       title = "Figure 5A: typical PK, 500 mg once daily")
p_pd <- ggplot(sim_typ, aes(time_rel, log10(parasites_plot), colour = arm)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(x = "Time after first dose (h)", y = "log10(parasites/mL)", colour = NULL,
       title = "Figure 5B: typical parasite count",
       caption = "Replicates Figure 5 of Krause 2016.")
p_pk
p_pd
```

The values below were read from Figure 5B. The typical solve is
deterministic, so the tolerances only absorb the reading error of the figure.

```{r fig5-check}
typ_summary <- sim_typ |>
  dplyr::group_by(arm) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    log10_at_dose = log10(parasites[time == t_dose1]),
    log10_at_288h = log10(parasites[time == t_dose1 + 288]),
    cmax_first_dose = max(Cc[time <= t_dose1 + 24]),
    h_to_cure = (time[cured][1]) - t_dose1,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    published_log10_at_288h = c(8.0, 4.6, 2.0, NA),
    published_h_to_cure = c(NA, NA, NA, 135)
  )
knitr::kable(typ_summary, digits = 2,
             caption = "Typical-value solve versus values read from Figure 5 of Krause 2016.")

stopifnot(
  # Pre-dose growth: log10 P rises from log10(0.11) to about 3.9 at dosing. A
  # misread growth-rate scale (G per hour vs percent per hour) misses by
  # hundreds of log units.
  all(abs(typ_summary$log10_at_dose - 3.9) < 0.15),
  # Figure 5A: first-dose peak just under 100 ng/mL.
  all(abs(typ_summary$cmax_first_dose - 98) < 8),
  # Figure 5B: log10 parasite count 288 h after the first dose for 1-3 doses.
  all(abs(typ_summary$log10_at_288h[1:3] - typ_summary$published_log10_at_288h[1:3]) < 0.4),
  # Figure 5B: only the four-dose regimen cures the typical subject, at
  # about 120-150 h.
  all(is.na(typ_summary$h_to_cure[1:3])),
  abs(typ_summary$h_to_cure[4] - 135) < 20
)
```

# Concentration-effect curve (Figure 3)

```{r fig3}
ini_vals <- rxode2::rxode(mod)$theta
emax <- exp(ini_vals[["lemax"]])
ec50 <- exp(ini_vals[["lec50"]])
hill <- exp(ini_vals[["lhill"]])
ce <- tibble::tibble(conc = seq(0, 100, by = 0.25)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(effect_pct_per_h = 100 * emax * conc^hill / (conc^hill + ec50^hill))
ggplot(ce, aes(conc, effect_pct_per_h)) +
  geom_line(colour = "steelblue") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 100 * emax, colour = "darkred") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = ec50, colour = "darkred") +
  labs(x = "ACT-451840 (ng/mL)", y = "Drug effect (growth rate reduction, %/h)",
       title = "Figure 3: concentration-effect curve",
       caption = "Replicates Figure 3 of Krause 2016.")
# The paper reports the effect as near-maximal from 10-15 ng/mL.
stopifnot(ce$effect_pct_per_h[ce$conc == 15] / (100 * emax) > 0.98)
```

# Stochastic cure prediction (Figures 4 and 6)

Figure 6 of Krause 2016 simulates 500 subjects for 1 to 6 once-daily doses of
500 mg and reports that fewer than 10% of subjects are cured by one dose, more
than half by four doses and more than 90% by six doses. The abstract adds that
six once-daily doses of 300 mg cure 90% of subjects. Each arm below has 200
virtual subjects.

```{r stoch-sim}
set.seed(4972157)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(4972157)
n_per_arm <- 200
arms <- tibble::tribble(
  ~n_dose, ~dose_mg,
  1, 500, 2, 500, 3, 500, 4, 500, 5, 500, 6, 500, 6, 300
)
ev_stoch <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(arms)), function(i) {
  make_arm(n_per_arm, arms$n_dose[i], arms$dose_mg[i], id_offset = (i - 1) * n_per_arm)
}))
sim_stoch <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = ev_stoch, keep = "arm") |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  apply_cure() |>
  dplyr::mutate(time_rel = time - t_dose1, arm = factor(arm, levels = unique(ev_stoch$arm)))
```

```{r fig6}
sim_stoch |>
  dplyr::group_by(arm, time_rel) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    q10 = quantile(log10(parasites_plot), 0.1),
    q50 = quantile(log10(parasites_plot), 0.5),
    q90 = quantile(log10(parasites_plot), 0.9),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time_rel, q50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = q10, ymax = q90), fill = "firebrick", alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_line(colour = "navy") +
  facet_wrap(~arm, nrow = 2) +
  labs(x = "Time after first dose (h)", y = "log10(parasites/mL)",
       title = "Figure 6: median and 10th-90th percentile parasite count",
       caption = "Replicates Figure 6 of Krause 2016 (plus a 6 x 300 mg arm).")
```

```{r fig4}
# Figure 4: single 500 mg dose, typical prediction and 80% interval.
sim_stoch |>
  dplyr::filter(arm == "1 x 500 mg") |>
  dplyr::group_by(time_rel) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    q10 = quantile(parasites, 0.1), q50 = quantile(parasites, 0.5),
    q90 = quantile(parasites, 0.9), .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time_rel, q50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = q10, ymax = q90), fill = "orchid", alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_line(colour = "purple4") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time after dose (h)", y = "Parasites/mL",
       title = "Figure 4: parasite count after a single 500 mg dose",
       caption = "Replicates the model band of Figure 4 of Krause 2016 (observed data not available).")
```

```{r cure-table}
cure <- sim_stoch |>
  dplyr::group_by(arm, id) |>
  dplyr::summarise(cured = any(cured), .groups = "drop") |>
  dplyr::group_by(arm) |>
  dplyr::summarise(pct_cured = 100 * mean(cured), .groups = "drop") |>
  dplyr::mutate(published = c("< 10%", "", "", "> 50%", "", "> 90%", "90%"))
cure |>
  dplyr::rename("Regimen" = arm, "Simulated % cured" = pct_cured,
                "Krause 2016 (Figure 6 text, abstract)" = published) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Percentage of virtual subjects cured (parasitaemia below 0.003/mL).")

pct <- setNames(cure$pct_cured, as.character(cure$arm))
# The published statements are thresholds on a 500-subject simulation; the
# bounds below leave several binomial standard errors (about 3.5 points at
# n = 200) of headroom on each side.
stopifnot(
  pct[["1 x 500 mg"]] < 15,
  pct[["4 x 500 mg"]] > 40,
  pct[["6 x 500 mg"]] > 80,
  pct[["6 x 300 mg"]] > 75
)
```

The 500 mg arms meet every threshold the paper states. Six doses of 300 mg cure
somewhat fewer virtual subjects than the 90% quoted in the abstract; the paper
does not show that simulation, so its size and variability settings are unknown.

# PKNCA validation

The paper reports a non-compartmental analysis of the eight observed profiles
after the single 500 mg dose (geometric mean AUC0-inf 1284.4 ng h/mL, Cmax
121.7 ng/mL, t1/2 36.4 h; median tmax 4 h). The block below runs PKNCA on 200
virtual subjects with the study's PK sampling times extended to 240 h.

```{r pknca-sim}
pk_times <- c(0, 0.5, 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, 20, 24, 48, 72, 96, 144, 192, 240)
ev_pk <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  tibble::tibble(id = 1:200, time = 0, evid = 1L, amt = 500, cmt = "depot"),
  tidyr::expand_grid(id = 1:200, time = pk_times) |>
    dplyr::mutate(evid = 0L, amt = 0, cmt = "parasites")
) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))
sim_pk <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = ev_pk) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  dplyr::mutate(treatment = "500 mg single dose")

sim_nca <- sim_pk |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, treatment)
sim_nca <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  sim_nca,
  sim_nca |> dplyr::distinct(id, treatment) |> dplyr::mutate(time = 0, Cc = 0)
) |>
  dplyr::distinct(id, treatment, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time)

dose_df <- tibble::tibble(id = 1:200, time = 0, amt = 500, treatment = "500 mg single dose")
conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(sim_nca, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | treatment + id)
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = 0, end = Inf,
  cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
```

```{r pknca-compare}
published <- data.frame(
  treatment = "500 mg single dose",
  cmax = 121.7, tmax = 4, aucinf.obs = 1284.4, half.life = 36.4
)
cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_res,
  reference = published,
  by = "treatment",
  units = c(cmax = "ng/mL", tmax = "h", aucinf.obs = "ng*h/mL", half.life = "h"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
cmp |>
  dplyr::rename("Treatment" = treatment) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = paste(
    "Simulated median NCA versus the observed NCA of Krause 2016 (geometric",
    "means; median for tmax). * differs by more than 20%."
  ))

nca_med <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  dplyr::group_by(PPTESTCD) |>
  dplyr::summarise(med = median(PPORRES, na.rm = TRUE))
med <- setNames(nca_med$med, nca_med$PPTESTCD)
stopifnot(
  # Exposure: a mis-transcribed volume, rate constant or unit moves AUC by
  # far more than this.
  abs(med[["aucinf.obs"]] / 1284.4 - 1) < 0.2,
  abs(med[["half.life"]] / 36.4 - 1) < 0.25,
  abs(med[["cmax"]] / 121.7 - 1) < 0.3
)
```

The simulated median Cmax is just under 20% below the observed geometric mean,
and the half-life about 10% shorter, while AUC and tmax agree. The packaged model reproduces the paper's own
typical-value simulation (Figure 5A peak just under 100 ng/mL), so the gap
lies between the fitted model and the observed NCA, not in the extraction.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Scale of G and D.** Table 1 prints the parasite growth rate G = 6.67 and
  the maximum kill rate D = 18.09 as 'unitless', and the Methods text describes
  G as a per-hour fraction (G = 0.1 is 10% per hour). Used as per-hour rate
  constants, the tabulated values would grow the inoculum by thousands of log
  units in 168 h. The values are percent per hour, so the model uses
  G = 0.0667 1/h and D = 0.1809 1/h. Figure 5B confirms the scale: the typical
  log10 parasite count rises from log10(0.11) = -0.96 at inoculation to about
  3.9 at dosing (ln(10) x 4.87 / 168 h = 0.067 1/h), and the y-axis of
  Figure 3, the drug effect expressed as growth-rate reduction, plateaus at 18.
  The typical-value checks above reproduce Figure 5 with this scale.
* **Random-effect distribution.** Table 1 gives the random effects as standard
  deviations without naming their distribution. They are encoded as log-normal
  (the Monolix default for positive parameters), with variance = SD^2.
* **Residual error form.** Table 1 gives an additive and a multiplicative term
  for each output. They are encoded as the Monolix 4.2 'combined1' form,
  SD = a + b x f (`combined1()`). The PK additive term (4.38e-9 ng/mL, RSE
  3.7e6%) is effectively zero, as the paper notes.
* **Time origin.** The paper places the inoculation at -168 h relative to the
  dose. The model starts at the inoculation (time 0, `parasites(0) = P0`), and
  the study dose is given at 168 h.
* **Cure threshold.** The 0.003 parasites/mL cure threshold is a simulation
  rule, not part of the ODE system; the model itself lets parasites regrow from
  any positive level. The vignette applies the rule after solving, holding a
  cured trajectory at the threshold as Figures 5B and 6 do.
* **Not modelled.** The ex vivo bioassay concentrations (antiparasitic activity
  expressed in ACT-451840 equivalents) were reported descriptively only. BLQ
  and below-LOD data were handled with the M3 method during estimation, which
  does not affect simulation. The rescue artemether/lumefantrine treatment is
  not part of the model.
* **No covariates.** The paper tested none; all eight subjects were healthy men.
* **Errata.** No erratum or correction for Krause 2016 was found in a Europe PMC
  search on 2026-11-24.
